name: Ammonia-soda manufacture
summary: From the 1830s works in Scotland, England and Belgium made soda from salt using ammonia to precipitate sodium bicarbonate; Solvay's Couillet works was operating by 1865.
description: Manufacture sodium carbonate or soda crystals from salt using an ammonium-carbonate reaction that precipitates sodium bicarbonate, which is then converted to the soda product. Later industrial variants recovered ammonia and used carbonating equipment; recovery is not asserted for every early attempt.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: Soda was in heavy demand for glass, soap and textiles, and the established Leblanc process was wasteful and polluting, so makers sought a cheaper route from salt.

places.note: Ambiguous English place name; assumed Newton, Lancashire (Newton-le-Willows) as in a sibling record

market.note: The sources describe manufacturing attempts and a later industrial soda-ash works; this does not establish a first sale.

date.label: by 1837

events.statement: At Turnbull and Ramsay’s Camlochie chemical works, John Thom produced soda from salt and ammonium carbonate by 1837, according to retrospective technical accounts.
events.scope: Manufacture of soda crystals from salt and ammonium carbonate via sodium bicarbonate, attributed to Thom’s work at Turnbull and Ramsay.
events.population: John Thom at the Turnbull and Ramsay chemical works
events.caveats: The 1885 account is retrospective and describes an imperfect technical manufacturing attempt; it reports about 100 kg per day and says the work was abandoned after about a year, whereas Hou gives 1837 and about 200 kg without a rate. The reports may concern the same attempt, but this is not proven. No customer sale, contemporary workers beyond the named chemist, ammonia recovery loop or sustained commercial success is established.
